transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for being here. As you know, we're reviewing the proposed plan to replace our seventh-grade humanities materials for the 2026-2027 school year. The draft currently proposes the Pathways Grade 6 edition, 80 printed copies, English-only materials, shared classroom-code digital access, one teacher workshop on August 12, and a student launch on August 17, 2026. I have final approval authority, but before I can finalize anything, I need to hear from each participating school function about their implementation requirements. Let's begin the reports. Who would like to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I've confirmed from the current teacher work agreement that implementation requires two paid preparation sessions — one on August 10 and one on August 12, 2026 — and that the earliest compliant student launch date is August 24, 2026. I should note that I have not yet entered these dates in the curriculum rollout calendar. This means the draft plan's single workshop on August 12 and student launch on August 17 would not be compliant with the agreement.
transcript.speaker: A5

transcript.text: I've reviewed the publisher's current license, and I need to flag a serious compliance issue with the draft plan. The license requires that the district provide one individually assigned digital account per student and one authorized print copy per student. It permits 96 print copies for this incoming cohort of 96 students — but the draft plan only proposes 80 printed copies, which falls short. Additionally, the license does not permit shared classroom-code digital access, which is what the draft currently proposes. We would need to revise both the print copy count up to 96 and switch from shared classroom-code access to individually assigned digital accounts to be compliant.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I've completed my enrollment review, and I need to flag a critical gap in the draft plan. I identified 14 students who require the Arabic version of the materials, in addition to students who use the Spanish version. I've confirmed with the publisher that both Spanish and Arabic editions are available for this resource. However, the language-service request has not yet been added to the adoption plan. The draft currently specifies English-only materials, which would not meet the needs of these students. We need to add Spanish and Arabic editions to the materials order to ensure all 96 students have access to appropriate resources.

Based on this direct classroom evidence, I recommend we revise the draft plan to specify the Pathways Grade 7 edition rather than the Grade 6 edition currently proposed.
